1: [Genesis Rabbah 8:4 — The angels debate the making of man]

When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create man, He took counsel with the ministering angels. He said to them: We will make man in our image. They said to Him: This man — what are his deeds? He said: His wisdom will surpass yours. He brought the animals before them and they could not name them; He brought them before Adam, who named each one.
[Genesis Rabbah 9:7 — A tale of two words]

Rabbi Simon ben Pazzi said: With the word 'Let there be' the world was spoken, yet the verse repeats it — 'Let there be light, and there was light.' Why the doubling? To teach that God created the light of this world and hid away the light of the world to come, for the righteous.

Rabbi Levi said: To what may Abraham be compared? To a man who was travelling from place to place and saw a palace in flames. He said: Can it be that this palace is without a master? The owner of the palace looked out and said: I am the master of the palace. So Abraham said: Can the world be without a Guide? And the Holy One said: I am the Guide of the world, its Master.
2: Rabbi Elazar said: When the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, wept. He said: Woe to the children on account of whose sins I destroyed My house and burnt My sanctuary and exiled them among the nations of the world.

Rabbi Eliezer brought every argument in the world to prove his case, but the sages would not accept them. A voice from heaven cried: Why do you dispute with Rabbi Eliezer, seeing that the law follows him in every place? Rabbi Joshua stood on his feet and said: It is not in heaven. The Torah is ours now — to study, to reason, to decide. That day the sages burned every ruling Rabbi Eliezer had made. Rabbi Eliezer wept, and the world was stricken — but the law was settled by human hands, as God had intended.

Therefore was man created alone: to teach you that whoever destroys a single soul of Israel, Scripture counts it as though he had destroyed a whole world; and whoever saves a single soul, Scripture counts it as though he had saved a whole world. And man was created alone for the sake of peace among people, that no one might say to another: My father was greater than your father.
3: [Exodus Rabbah 31:17 — The cry of the oppressed]

Rabbi Phinehas said: You find that wherever Israel was oppressed, the Divine Spirit rested upon them. Is it not written: In all their affliction He was afflicted? He does not say 'their affliction' but 'affliction' — as if to say, the affliction of all of them, of every people.

Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Aibu: Neither this world nor the world to come was made save for the sake of those who say, 'Hear, O Israel.' And just as salt flavours meat, so does the Torah flavour the world. If the Torah were not in the world, the world would have returned to chaos and void.
[Midrash Tehillim on Psalm 133 — How good it is]

How good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity — like the precious oil upon the head. What is unity worth? It is like the dew of Hermon. For see what unity does: it turns a mountain of division into a meadow, and strangers into a single house.
